anti_patterns: Don't create a separate ObservableObject for each facet — one object can have multiple facets
Don't use Tool as a top-level evidence item — it describes the instrument, not the evidence
Don't model the phone as an InvestigativeAction — the phone is an ObservableObject, the extraction is the action
Don't flatten app data into one facet — use separate facets for messages, contacts, call logs
Don't flatten the sysdiagnose tree into one File observable — keep logarchive and high-value children linked
Don't invent a SysdiagnoseFacet — use FileFacet directories plus AppleUnifiedLogArchive
Don't invent UnifiedLogFacet — map rows with EventRecordFacet and Dictionary attributes
Don't claim message text without running a parser on the binary logarchive
Don't model sender and recipient as the same ObservableObject — use separate EmailAddressFacet instances
Don't skip the EmailAccountFacet when account-level metadata is available
Don't omit the Tool object — always record which tool (and version) performed the action
Don't model tool output without linking it to the InvestigativeAction that produced it
mapping_guide_patterns.code_skeleton:
tool = graph.create(Tool, name=..., version=...)
action = graph.create(InvestigativeAction, name=..., instrument=tool)

anti_patterns: Don't model each packet as a separate ObservableObject — group by connection or flow
Don't put IP addresses in NetworkConnectionFacet text fields — use separate IPAddressFacet objects
Don't confuse ImageFacet (disk image metadata) with picture/photo image data
Don't skip ContentDataFacet — hash values are critical for disk image integrity
Don't model each URL visit as a separate ObservableObject — use URLHistoryFacet entries
Don't forget ApplicationFacet to identify which browser produced the history

mapping_guide_patterns.pattern: InvestigativeAction (per pipeline step) + AnalyticTool + RasterPicture + ConfidenceFacet + Relationship
anti_patterns: Don't hide structured facts (model name, query, thresholds, scores) inside uco-core:description as JSON strings — use explicit properties or ConfiguredTool
Don't use ArtifactClassification for tool endpoint names — classification describes what the artifact IS (content label), not which tool processed it
Don't model a multi-step pipeline as a single InvestigativeAction — each model/step gets its own action with its own inputs, outputs, and timestamps
Don't use generic File or ObservableObject for image files — use RasterPicture with RasterPictureFacet
Don't omit per-result scores — use ConfidenceFacet on each result for ranking and explainability
Don't omit hashes and sizes on evidence files — without them the graph is a workflow log, not an evidentiary record
mapping_guide_patterns.code_skeleton:
# One InvestigativeAction per pipeline step
step = graph.create(InvestigativeAction, name=..., instrument=[tool], object=[inputs], result=[outputs])
# RasterPicture with score
img = graph.create(RasterPicture, has_facet=[FileFacet(...), ContentDataFacet(hash=[...]), RasterPictureFacet(...), ConfidenceFacet(confidence=0.87)])
# Explicit relationship
graph.create(Relationship, source=[img], target=input_dir, kind_of_relationship='Selected_From', is_directional=True)

anti_patterns: Don't model registry values without their parent key — always include the key path
Don't use generic FileFacet for registry hive content — use the specific registry facets

mapping_guide_patterns.source: child sex trafficking ring or recruitment network
mapping_guide_patterns.pattern: CACInvestigation + TraffickingEnterprise + (TraffickingRing | TraffickingCell) + TraffickingVictimRole + (PeerRecruitmentNetwork | ClassmateRecruitmentNetwork) + (SchoolBasedRecruitment | StreetBasedRecruitment with pretext approach) + DigitalToPhysicalBridge
anti_patterns: Don't model a trafficking ring as a single Identity — use TraffickingEnterprise (or TraffickingRing/TraffickingCell) so role hierarchy and victim relationships have a structural anchor
Don't reuse generic InvestigativeAction for each pretext approach — use the specific *OfferApproach subclass so analysts can query approach patterns
Don't treat 'online recruitment then in-person meet' as one event — split it: one online behavior event plus a DigitalToPhysicalBridge for the meet, so the timeline shows the transition
Don't forget to set CASE_UCO_EXTENSIONS=cac so trafficking and recruitment classes load
mapping_guide_patterns.code_skeleton:
# Requires CASE_UCO_EXTENSIONS=cac
ring = graph.create(TraffickingRing, name='Ring 2026-014')
victim_role = graph.create(MinorTraffickingVictimRole, name='Victim A role')
approach = graph.create(TransportationOfferApproach, name='Bus-stop ride offer')
bridge = graph.create(DigitalToPhysicalBridge, name='IG DM -> motel meet')
graph.create(Relationship, source=[approach], target=[victim_role], kind_of_relationship='Targeted')

mapping_guide_patterns.source: multi-jurisdictional rescue or task force operation
mapping_guide_patterns.pattern: CACInvestigation + TaskForce + (LocalJurisdiction | StateJurisdiction | FederalJurisdiction | InternationalJurisdiction) + JointInvestigation + (MassChildRescueOperation | VictimExtraction) + JurisdictionalHandoff + MutualAidRequest
anti_patterns: Don't model the task force as a generic Identity — use TaskForce so participating jurisdictions/agencies have a structural relationship
Don't bury jurisdictional transitions in a description string — use JurisdictionalHandoff (and MutualAidRequest where relevant) so the chain is queryable
Don't lose per-victim provenance during a mass rescue — pair MassChildRescueOperation with one VictimExtraction per victim, each with its own ProvenanceRecord
mapping_guide_patterns.code_skeleton:
# Requires CASE_UCO_EXTENSIONS=cac
tf = graph.create(TaskForce, name='Regional ICAC Task Force')
op = graph.create(MassChildRescueOperation, name='Operation Lighthouse')
fed = graph.create(FederalJurisdiction, name='HSI - Field Office X')
state = graph.create(StateJurisdiction, name='State Police')
graph.create(JurisdictionalHandoff, source=[state], target=[fed], name='Lead transferred to HSI')

mapping_guide_patterns.pattern: CACInvestigation + (ArrestOperation | HighRiskArrest) + DynamicEntry + SuspectProfile + ThreatAssessment + AssetForfeitureAction
anti_patterns: Don't collapse pre-op planning and the entry into one action — pre-op SuspectProfile/ThreatAssessment justify the operational posture and need their own records
Don't model seized property as plain ObservableObject — use AssetForfeitureAction so the legal-process linkage is explicit
mapping_guide_patterns.code_skeleton:
# Requires CASE_UCO_EXTENSIONS=cac
ta = graph.create(ThreatAssessment, name='Pre-op threat assessment')
arrest = graph.create(HighRiskArrest, name='Arrest of subject X')
entry = graph.create(DynamicEntry, name='Front-door dynamic entry')
forfeiture = graph.create(AssetForfeitureAction, name='Vehicle and electronics seizure')

mapping_guide_patterns.source: victim rescue extraction and post-rescue services
mapping_guide_patterns.pattern: CACInvestigation + EmergencyResponse + VictimExtraction + OngoingDangerAssessment + SafetyPlanning + MultiAgencyVictimResponse + TraumaIndicator + HelpSeekingBarrier
anti_patterns: Don't treat post-rescue services as out-of-scope — model MultiAgencyVictimResponse and SafetyPlanning so downstream services are auditable

Don't conflate recantation with case closure — RecantationAssessment is its own event and may coexist with an ongoing investigation; pair it with ReaffirmedDisclosureStatement when the disclosure is later reaffirmed
mapping_guide_patterns.code_skeleton:
# Requires CASE_UCO_EXTENSIONS=cac
extraction = graph.create(VictimExtraction, name='Victim extraction at motel')
danger = graph.create(OngoingDangerAssessment, name='Trafficker still at-large')

mapping_guide_patterns.source: csam provenance forensics and victim identification
mapping_guide_patterns.pattern: ForensicAcquisitionAction + ChainOfCustodyAction (per event) + EvidenceVerificationAction + (MetadataCorrelation | TemporalPatternAnalysis | GeospatialCorrelation | CrossPlatformCorrelation | BehavioralFingerprinting) + VictimIdentificationProcess
anti_patterns: Don't merge acquisition, verification, and analysis into one action — each is its own auditable step with its own tool, operator, and timestamp
Don't omit hashes on CSAM artifacts — without ContentDataFacet entries the chain of custody is unverifiable
Don't store correlation findings only in description text — use the matching CAC correlation class so the result is queryable
mapping_guide_patterns.code_skeleton:
# Requires CASE_UCO_EXTENSIONS=cac
acq = graph.create(ForensicAcquisitionAction, name='Acquisition of seized device')
verify = graph.create(EvidenceVerificationAction, name='SHA-256 verification')
img = graph.create(RasterPicture, has_facet=[FileFacet(file_name=...), ContentDataFacet(hash_method='SHA-256', hash_value='...'), RasterPictureFacet(...)])
vid = graph.create(VictimIdentificationProcess, name='Match against known-victim DB')

mapping_guide_patterns.pattern: CACInvestigation + MarylandICACtaskForce + InvestigativeAction chain + Authorization + ArrestOperation (warrant_arrest) + BookingAction + CorrectionalFacility + StateCharge
anti_patterns: Don't use HighRiskArrest or DynamicEntry when the narrative says custody was without incident
Don't duplicate MSP CCU as both a specialized unit and a separate performer Organization
Don't leave OnlineGrooming or OnlinePurchase isolated — add uco-action:performer (suspect) and investigation Concerns links
Don't create empty Phase nodes — use typed phases with occursDuringPhase on actions or omit phases
Don't embed ExternalReference as a blank node — give it an explicit @id IRI
Don't put grooming events in Investigation.uco-core:object — reserve object for ObservableObject evidence

mapping_guide_patterns.pattern: CACInvestigation + GroomingBehavior + NCMECCybertipReport + GroomingMessage + ChildVictim + OnlinePredator
anti_patterns: Don't use generic InvestigativeAction for grooming phases — use GroomingBehavior with grooming stage properties from the CAC extension
Don't model the CyberTip as a plain ObservableObject — use NCMECCybertipReport with incident type and annotations from the CAC extension
Don't use freetext descriptions for grooming phases — use the structured GroomingPhase classes (InitialContactPhase, TrustBuildingPhase, etc.)
Don't forget to set CASE_UCO_EXTENSIONS=cac to load CAC classes in the MCP server
mapping_guide_patterns.code_skeleton:
# Requires CASE_UCO_EXTENSIONS=cac
# CAC grooming + NCMEC classes
grooming = graph.create(OnlineGrooming, name=..., grooming_stage='trust_building')
victim = graph.create(ChildVictim, name=...)
offender = graph.create(OnlinePredator, name=...)
cybertip = graph.create(NCMECCybertipReport, name=...)
# Link to core UCO messaging
thread = graph.create(MessageThread, has_facet=[MessageThreadFacet(participant=[offender_acct, victim_acct])])

core_patterns.name: ObservableObject + Facets
core_patterns.description: The most common pattern. Create an ObservableObject and attach one or more Facets to describe it. A single observable can have multiple facets (e.g., FileFacet + ContentDataFacet for a file with its hash).
core_patterns.python_example:
graph.create(ObservableObject, has_facet=[
    FileFacet(file_name='evidence.dd', size_in_bytes=1073741824),
    ContentDataFacet(hash_method='SHA-256', hash_value='abc123...'),
])

core_patterns.name: Investigation + Action + Tool
core_patterns.description: Model a forensic workflow: an Investigation contains InvestigativeActions, each performed by a Tool that produces ObservableObjects as output.
core_patterns.python_example:
inv = graph.create(Investigation, name='Case 2024-001')
tool = graph.create(Tool, name='Autopsy', version='4.21.0')
action = graph.create(InvestigativeAction, name='Disk analysis')

core_patterns.name: Identity + Role
core_patterns.description: Associate a person or organization with a role in the investigation (examiner, subject, witness).
core_patterns.python_example:
person = graph.create(Identity, name='Jane Smith')
role = graph.create(Role, name='Lead Examiner')

core_patterns.name: Provenance + Chain of Custody
core_patterns.description: Track evidence handling with ProvenanceRecord and sequential InvestigativeActions for each custody event.
core_patterns.python_example:
record = graph.create(ProvenanceRecord,
    description='Evidence received from field office')
